Aditya / Marissa — looked into INV-20270622. Short answer: credits issued through our PLG self-serve (signup voucher) are accounted for as a contra-revenue item, not a separate supply, but EU VAT treatment can vary by jurisdiction and by whether the credit is a discount versus a taxable supply. From the invoice breakdown:

- Line 1: Usage 06/20–06/21 — EUR 1,200.00
- Line 2: Promotional credit (signup trial) — EUR -400.00
- Subtotal: EUR 800.00
- VAT (20% GB example) — EUR 160.00
- Total: EUR 960.00

Our system currently calculates VAT on the net after credits. For many customers that is appropriate when credits are considered a discount to the taxable supply. However — since NovusAI is an EU-registered business and provided a VAT number in the account, we should have zero-rated the VAT or indicated reverse-charge (depending on country), not charged VAT on the net. That was a configuration miss for their account (their VAT number was present but VAT handling didn't apply due to a flag mismatch).

What I propose:
1) Reissue corrected invoice INV-20270622-corrected.pdf showing VAT 0% with a note "Reverse charge — customer VAT applied" (or the appropriate mechanism per country).
2) Do NOT issue a cash refund; instead issue the corrected invoice and post an accounting credit so their ledger shows correct VAT treatment.
3) As a courtesy for the disruption, extend their remaining promotional trial credit by 100k tokens (one-time) and add a line item memo in the invoice metadata.

I can coordinate with finance to generate the corrected invoice and post the journal entries — need confirmation from you (Aditya) to proceed and approval to add the courtesy token extension. We should get this done before Jul 2.

— Vivek

- Posted an accounting credit so the original charge will be offset and your ledger will match the corrected invoice — no cash refund required unless you request one.
